description: I’m Anis Bellil, a full-stack developer and teacher. You don't need years of experience to contribute—just curiosity and a willingness to dive in. Whether you're a student starting out in IT or someone eager to explore a new field, come build with us. Let’s tackle this hackathon together and make the most of the experience.
summary: An astronaut health monitor built in React, with no backend. It tracks sixteen metrics against normal, warning and critical ranges, and shows NASA’s five spaceflight hazards through a body map, hazard bar, toast alerts and a live log. A mission simulator drifts metrics over time to demonstrate how threats escalate.
details:
Astronaut Health Monitor

Browser app that tracks an astronaut’s vital and wellness signs and warns when NASA’s five spaceflight hazards start to emerge.

Problem: crews far from Earth can’t count on quick medical help, so small changes in sleep, heart rate or environment need to be caught early and explained clearly.

Solution

  • Metrics: 15 of them, each with its own normal, warning and critical ranges.
  • Body map: head, chest, heart, arms and legs, colored by their worst metric.
  • Hazard bar: NASA’s five hazards (Isolation & Confinement, Space Radiation, Gravity Fields, Hostile & Closed Environments, Distance from Earth). Four are levels, and Distance from Earth shows a number (400 km at the station, 384,400 km at the Moon, 55-400 million km at Mars).
  • Hazard rule: a hazard changes only when all of its metrics reach a level, and the lowest metric decides.
  • Alerts: a toast with the advised action fires when a metric rises to warning or critical, or a hazard escalates.
  • Log: a timestamped log with type filters.
  • Controls: sliders for every metric.
  • Simulator: a mission clock (1x to 24x, pause and reset) with five scenarios that push a hazard’s metrics toward critical.

Metrics by hazard

  • Space Radiation: headache, sleep deficit, heart rate, stress (HRV), breathing rate, energy.
  • Gravity Fields: dizziness, bone & muscle loss, vision acuity, weight loss.
  • Hostile & Closed Environments: microbiome diversity, Proteobacteria, Akkermansia.
  • Isolation & Confinement: red blood cells, white blood cells, IgG.

Tech: React with Tailwind CSS and react-toastify. There is no backend and no database. All metric ranges and hazards are plain data in one JS file.

Limits to state honestly

  • The ranges are general clinical references, not NASA-validated.
  • All data is simulated.
  • The anomaly AI model is built but not integrated into the app.
  • It is a prototype for awareness, not medical advice.
